title: Catch OSError during ZoneInfo string validation
answers: Why does ZoneInfo validation crash with OSError instead of ValidationError?
How should ZoneInfo instantiation errors be handled when validating timezone strings?
Why does validating timezone strings like 'America' or long strings fail with unhandled OSError?
body:
Symptom: Validating timezone strings such as 'America' or long strings crashes with an unhandled OSError instead of raising a ValidationError.
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_validators.py:validate_str_is_valid_iana_tz caught (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, TypeError) but omitted OSError when instantiating ZoneInfo(value).
Fix pattern: Catch OSError alongside ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, and TypeError, and raise PydanticCustomError('zoneinfo_str', 'invalid timezone: {value}', {'value': value}).
Constraints: Applies when initializing ZoneInfo from raw string inputs where filesystem-backed timezone lookups can fail; does not apply to already-constructed ZoneInfo instances.
applies: Validation of string inputs into zoneinfo.ZoneInfo objects
